leads.title: Matteo Niccolini (Rome) → Dieci, ciphered copy sent on to Machiavelli in France, with the Dieci's covering letter almost entirely in cipher
leads.correspondents: Matteo Niccolini (Florentine orator, Rome) → Dieci di Balìa, copy forwarded to Niccolò Machiavelli; Dieci di Balìa → Machiavelli (at the French court)
leads.shelfmark: BNCF, Carte Machiavelli V/140 (enclosure) and V/139 (covering letter)
leads.folio_note: V/140: 2 ff., whole letter in cipher (copy, no place or signature); V/139: 2 ff., almost all in cipher except the first two lines, line 3 deciphered interlinear; on V/139 ff. 1v-2r Machiavelli's own decipherment of V/140, described by BNCF as 'inexact and incomplete'
leads.status: BNCF catalogue (Internet Culturale, 2009): V/140 'La lettera è in cifra'; V/139 'quasi interamente in cifra ... la terza riga è decifrata in interlinea'; Machiavelli's decipherment of V/140 'inesatta ed incompleta'. Not on DECODE (known.py (your repo + DECODE + Cryptoole list) 'Carte Machiavelli', 'Machiavelli V': no hits). Printed: Bertelli, Legazioni e commissarie (Feltrinelli 1964) pp. 1280-81 no. 30 (V/139) and pp. 1352-53 app. A (V/140); Opere (1877) VI pp. 53-55. Whether Bertelli prints a full reading of the cipher (from the ASF register or the Rome original) is not checked.
leads.why: The Florentine chancery cipher of 1510 seen at work in Machiavelli's French legation (Julius II's turn against France); Machiavelli's own faulty decipherment is a rare view of a secretary decoding on mission.
